overall_reason: A deliberate console-dashboard concept (PS5-style hero art, cover carousel, controller legend) that no landing-page prompt would produce, but executed with AI-default finishes (violet-to-cyan gradient buttons, glow ring, gradient 'made with' credit, stock catalog copy) and visibly unreviewed collisions at desktop width.

findings.evidence: 'PLAY' is a violet-to-magenta gradient pill and '$0.49' cart button is a cyan-to-blue gradient; 'Subscribe' is a cyan pill; the selected cover has a cyan glow ring. These are the violet/cyan defaults rather than colours drawn from the console theme or game art.
findings.before: Violet gradient PLAY + cyan gradient cart + cyan glow focus ring
findings.after: One flat action colour taken from the brand (the GG ghost mark is white on black) and a plain white selection ring like the console UI being referenced
findings.why: Purple/cyan gradient pairs with glow are the strongest machine-default colour tell (SLP-007, SLP-008, look family violet-gradient).

findings.where: hero info block over carousel, 1440 tile 00
findings.evidence: At 1440 the cover carousel sits on top of the 'PLAY' and 'ADD TO CART — $0.49' buttons, the 'FEATURED GAMES' label overprints 'Follow game', and 'Enter Fullscreen' overprints 'Install App'. The layout was not checked at this width.
findings.after: Reserve the carousel's height below the action row (e.g. grid rows: info / actions / carousel) so nothing overlaps at 1280-1440
findings.why: Unreviewed overlap is the signature of generated output shipped without a look; it also hides the main CTA.

findings.evidence: Failed T-FRESH-READER: "Experience intense multiplayer combat with a variety of weapons, power-ups, and game modes", "delivers classic arena shooter gameplay with modern graphics and responsive controls", "Refine the catalog without leaving the action."
findings.before: "Experience intense multiplayer combat with a variety of weapons, power-ups, and game modes."
findings.after: Concrete facts: [DATA NEEDED: modes, player count, what runs in-browser and how long it takes to load]
findings.why: Store-blurb filler that would fit any shooter page.

findings.evidence: "made with ♥ by Alex St. Louis for gamers everywhere" set in mono with a multi-stop gradient fill (sweep gradient hit) and purple heart.
findings.after: Plain text credit in the UI face, or remove
findings.why: 'Made with love' gradient credit line is a vibe-coded template residue; deleting it loses nothing (T-DELETION).

findings.evidence: Five consecutive covers badged 'NEW GAME' (sweep repeated_label) including Xonotic (2011) and The Simpsons: Hit & Run; badges carry no information.
findings.after: Badge only what is actually new this week, with a date, or drop the badge
findings.why: A label on everything is a label on nothing; misleading 'new' on a 2011 game.

strengths: The concept is specific and chosen: a console-home metaphor with full-bleed game art, an ESRB rating plate, keyboard/gamepad legend ('SELECT / ROW / LAUNCH') and a cover-flow row. Keep the console idea.
Mobile adapts the metaphor ('Tap to Select | Swipe to Navigate') rather than collapsing to a generic list.
not_investigated: Exo 2 display font and theme audio were blocked (manifest network); typography judged on the fallback face only.
Background is a video/animated scene seen as a still; motion not judged.
Rights to commercial game covers (Simpsons, Super Monkey Ball, Stormgate) are outside this lens.
